summary: Periodic tail-latency regressions after quiet-window resume causing streaming timeouts
description:
Issue summary: Since 2026-03-09 21:00 UTC BeaconAI has reported intermittent periodic p95->p99 latency waves that correlate with connection/activity resumption after quiet periods. Impact: Customers observe 5xx timeouts and streaming disconnects during the p99 windows; affects several production endpoints for BeaconAI (enterprise).

Environment: prod us-east-1, majority of traffic routed through our US East API gateway to dedicated GPU pools. Models: rw-infer-13B-quant primarily; occasional rw-infer-70B.

Symptoms observed: multiple ~20-45s long tail-latency waves every ~5-15 minutes followed by normal operation. P95 remains stable but p99 spikes to 8-12s and some requests time out at client-side at 30s. Streaming sessions occasionally cut with ECONNRESET. Metrics show a rise in per-shard batch window (linger) and sudden coalescing of long-requests behind short request bursts at the moment of traffic resume.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Idle a stable connection pattern for ~3-10 minutes 2) Resume a burst of short streaming requests (avg 6 tokens per call) 3) Observe an amplified linger flush causing a super-batch that blocks KV cache warmup and increases token generation latency for concurrent requests.

Logs / traces: Correlated traces in X-Ray show requests queued in batcher queue for ~400-1200ms before dispatch, then kernel queueing of ~1.2-3s for rw-infer-13B-quant. Serving runtime logs show "coalesce_window_extended" events and batcher metrics show sudden cohort flush sizes 3-5x above normal. No error level exceptions in runtime; mostly backpressure and increased serialization time.

Initial hypothesis: On quiet->resume transitions the batcher linger heuristic is overshooting due to an outdated idle-epoch timestamp combined with tenant-priority reshuffle, which causes a few streams to accumulate into a large flush. The large flush increases KV cache miss penalty for newly resumed prefixes and causes downstream kernel contention. This creates a transient p99 tail until batches return to steady state.

Immediate mitigations attempted: 1) Support applied request-level retry guidance to BeaconAI to reduce client-side timeouts (temporary). 2) SRE adjusted batcher conservative linger cap on a small subset of shards (canary) which reduced wave amplitude by ~40% in canary. 3) Temporary routing to alternate dedicated pool for a subset of traffic to avoid noisy neighbor amplification.

Open action items: - Product to consider adding explicit quiet-resume detector to force fast flush of small batches on resume. - Engineering to instrument per-tenant idle-epoch and tie to linger cap. - Runbook update to include known mitigation steps and when to move traffic to alternate pools.

Impact statement: Affects customer throughput during resume windows and may degrade SLAs for streaming endpoints; customer-visible errors have been reduced after canary but root cause fix required to prevent recurrence.

2026-03-10 11:45 - Marcus Nguyen (SRE): Observed linger cap explosion on shard-42 around timestamps customer provided. Started canary with linger_cap=30ms and monitored.
2026-03-10 15:02 - BeaconAI (Customer): Confirming that after the routing change some streaming sessions improved but occasional timeouts still happen. Asked for ETA on permanent fix.

2026-03-11 07:20 - Evelyn Chen (Runtime): Found a race in idle-epoch update path where resume events reset epoch incorrectly for reshuffled tenants, allowing linger to grow beyond configured caps for a short period.

2026-03-11 16:30 - Marcus Nguyen (SRE): Canary metrics: p99 reduced by ~40% for canary shards; overall incidence lowered but not eliminated. Preparing PR to add explicit quiet-resume detector and epoch sanity checks.
resolution: Mitigation in progress: canary linger cap adjustment and routing to alternate pool reduced customer-visible errors. Engineering PR prepared to add resume detector and fix epoch race; deployment planned to canary on 2026-03-14. Post-deploy we will monitor p99 for 72 hours and update runbook. Customer notified of timeline and temporary workarounds.
